app_note: Citric acid gives a clean sour taste and helps keep foods in the intended acidity range.
risk_note: Usually used for taste and acidity balance rather than as a vitamin source.

app_note: Malic acid is strongly associated with the tart flavor of apples and sour candies.
risk_note: Can taste sharper and longer-lasting than citric acid.

app_note: Tartaric acid occurs in grapes and is also used in some baking systems and sour foods.
risk_note: Usually low concern at normal food-use levels.

app_note: Fumaric acid provides a strong sour taste and is common in dry sour flavor systems.
risk_note: May taste more persistent than citric acid in candies.

app_note: Lactic acid is produced in many fermented foods and can also be added for tangy acidity.
risk_note: Despite the name it is not necessarily dairy-derived.

app_note: Acetic acid is the main acid associated with vinegar flavor.
risk_note: Food labels may list vinegar or acetic acid depending on the product.

app_note: Phosphoric acid gives cola-style drinks a distinctive sharp acidity.
risk_note: Phosphate intake context should be handled separately from taste function.

app_note: Sodium citrate buffers acidity and helps processed cheese melt smoothly.
risk_note: Adds sodium and should be counted in sodium-aware views.

app_note: Potassium citrate buffers acidity and can contribute potassium.
risk_note: People tracking potassium should notice added potassium salts.

app_note: Calcium citrate can be used as a calcium source and acidity regulator.
risk_note: Mineral amount matters more than the ingredient name alone.

app_note: Baking soda is a classic leavening ingredient for quick breads cookies and cakes.
risk_note: Adds sodium and can taste soapy if a recipe is not balanced.

app_note: Monocalcium phosphate is a common acidic component in baking powders.
risk_note: It helps baking powder provide reliable rise.

app_note: SAPP is used in baking powders and prepared baked goods for controlled rise.
Cream of tartar is potassium bitartrate from wine production and is common in baking.
Sodium aluminum phosphate is used in some baking powders and baking mixes.
risk_note: Flag as aluminum-containing for users who want to filter it.

app_note: Calcium carbonate can provide calcium and act as a mineral ingredient in foods.
risk_note: Can feel chalky in some products if not formulated well.

app_note: Potassium carbonate is used in some foods where alkalinity affects texture color or flavor.
